site.name: pulsegrid
site.summary: PulseGrid Fictional bulk-power-system SCADA / EMS dashboard "PulseGrid" for the Western Interconnect. UXBench fixture in the Dashboard category. Pages - `index.html` — **Overview**. Left rail nav (6 entries with alarm badge); top bar with BA selector (Western / ERCOT / SPP / MISO), Production / Replay / Plan tabs, live ticking clock, ⌘K, theme toggle, alert bell, operator avatar; 5 KPI cards (demand / generation / frequency / renewables share / active alarms) each with sparkline; **2-column body grid**: 48-hour load chart with actual / forecast (dashed) / net renewables area + "NOW" marker, weather card with 4 zones (Phoenix 112°F driving 1.8 GW cooling load, Tehachapi wind, etc.), 24-cell generator status grid (color-coded online / tripped / ramping / maintenance with output + % capacity), active-alarms list with severity dots (critical pulses), live fuel-mix bars (7 fuels), interchange table with 6 tie-lines (sched / actual / Δ). - `generators.html` — **Generator list** (38 units across the fleet). Filter strip with status pills (All / Online / Ramping / Tripped / Maintenance), fuel and zone selectors, and search. Sortable-style table with EMS ID, plant name, fuel-color icon, zon

run_plan.goal: Explore PulseGrid’s main operator dashboard and verify the adjacent fleet, forecast, and alarm workflows across desktop and mobile, with emphasis on state changes, filtering, and recovery paths.
run_plan.summary: Start on the Overview dashboard to confirm the top-level operational picture, then branch into the generator list, forecast view, and alarms queue using the visible navigation and in-page links. Focus on how the dashboard’s controls behave (BA selector, Production/Replay/Plan tabs, time-range toggles, status filters, search, and alarm actions), and use those pages to check whether detail/state transitions are clear and consistent. Repeat the most important interactions on mobile viewport because several navigation and header controls were flagged as small tap targets, and the BA selector lacks an input label. Avoid assuming hidden topology/events functionality beyond the placeholder links seen in the prescan.
assumptions: Topology and Events were present in navigation but only shown as '#' placeholders in the prescan, so they should be treated as non-functional or out of scope unless they reveal real content during execution.
The four known HTML pages are the full reachable surface for this run: index.html, generators.html, forecast.html, and alarms.html.
The left-rail nav and top-bar controls are shared enough that issues found on one page may recur on the others.
The visible alert counts and labels are meaningful for UX validation, but the exact SCADA data values are fixture content rather than live system truth.
risk_hotspots: index.html: BA selector with missing label/accessible name concerns and small tap targets in the top bar.
index.html: Production / Replay / Plan tabs and time-range buttons (24h, 48h, 7d) because they appear to drive core operational context.
index.html: Active alarms preview and the 'All alarms →' / 'View all 312 →' drill-down links.
generators.html: Search field, status pills, fuel/zone selectors, and the large generator table with many rows and mixed states (online, ramping, tripped, maintenance).
forecast.html: Model/timescale selector and the hourly breakdown rows that are described as tappable overlays.
alarms.html: Acknowledge selected action, severity/status/time filters, filter input, checkbox selection, and per-row Open/Acked/Resolved actions.
Mobile viewport: multiple navigation buttons and header controls are under 44px tall, creating likely touch usability risk.

phases.title: Baseline dashboard verification
phases.objective: Validate the Overview page as the primary operator landing surface and confirm the visible cross-system status, charts, and summary cards behave coherently.
key_checks: Inspect the five KPI cards for readable state, trend indicators, and consistency with the visible alarm/demand/generation context.
Switch the system load chart between 24h, 48h, and 7d and confirm the chart and NOW marker update without layout breakage.
Review generator-status summary tiles, active alarms preview, fuel mix, and interchange table for internal consistency and drill-in affordances.
Check the BA selector, Production/Replay/Plan tabs, clock/theme/bell/command button, and note whether any of them visibly change state.
exit_criteria: All major visible Overview regions have been inspected at least once.
At least one time-range toggle and one top-bar control have been exercised.
Any obvious accessibility or interaction anomalies on the landing page have been recorded.

phases.title: Generator fleet navigation and filtering
phases.objective: Validate the fleet list as the main drill-down from the dashboard and verify filtering, search, and row-level information density.
key_checks: Open the generator list from the left nav and/or the 'View all 312 →' link to confirm consistent routing.
Exercise the status pills (All, Online, Ramping, Tripped, Maintenance) and verify the table contents respond appropriately.
Use the fuel and zone selectors plus the search field to narrow the list and observe whether counts/table rows update predictably.
Inspect a sample of rows across different states, especially tripped and maintenance units, to check clarity of status, capacity, output, operator, and details affordance.
exit_criteria: At least three filter combinations have been tested, including one search-driven narrowing.
A representative sample of generator states has been inspected.
The page’s table and controls are confirmed usable at desktop and then rechecked on mobile viewport.

phases.title: Forecast scenario and horizon checks
phases.objective: Validate the forecast page’s model context, horizon controls, and hourly breakdown interactions for planning-style review.
key_checks: Confirm the model metadata, day-ahead/hour-ahead/real-time selector, and peak/reserve context are visible and understandable.
Toggle the 12h, 24h, and 7d horizon buttons and verify the chart and summary figures remain coherent.
Interact with several hourly breakdown rows to see whether row selection/overlay behavior is discoverable and stable.
Check the reserve adequacy warnings around higher forecast hours and whether they are legible at a glance.
exit_criteria: At least one model selector state and one horizon state have been exercised.
Multiple hourly rows have been inspected for interaction clarity.
No chart/control rendering issues appear when switching horizons.

phases.title: Alarm triage and recovery workflow
phases.objective: Validate the alarms queue as the main operational recovery path, including filtering, selection, and acknowledge flows.
key_checks: Open the alarms page and verify the active/critical/resolved summary counts and mean-handle-time KPI.
Test severity, status, and time filters, plus the free-text filter input, to confirm the list can be narrowed in a controlled way.
Select one or more alarms and evaluate whether 'Acknowledge selected' reflects the current selection state appropriately.
Inspect row-level actions and status labels for open, acked, and resolved alarms, especially the critical COL-3 and WND-12 entries.
exit_criteria: All visible filter classes have been tried at least once.
At least one selection-based action path has been tested.
The alarm list’s triage workflow is understandable without hidden behavior.

phases.title: Mobile viewport regression pass
phases.objective: Repeat the most critical task flows in a narrow viewport to validate touch usability and responsive stability.
key_checks: Revisit the left navigation, top bar controls, and primary filters to confirm the small-tap-target warnings are user-impacting on mobile.
Repeat one high-value action per page: chart range toggle on Overview, filter/search on Generators, horizon toggle on Forecast, and alarm filtering/selection on Alarms.
Check whether any control labels, tables, or charts overflow or become difficult to operate in mobile layout.
exit_criteria: Critical interactions have been replayed in mobile viewport on all known pages.
Responsive issues are categorized by impact rather than only recorded as generic warnings.
Any unusable control on mobile is tied to its exact page and interaction.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages (4/4) and validate the main entry, list, planning, and triage flows.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on each key page, including navigation, selectors, filters, chart horizon toggles, search, and at least one row-level or action-level interaction where present.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the highest-value interactions on mobile viewport, prioritizing the header/nav controls and one primary workflow per page.

notes: Treat the placeholder Topology and Events nav items as exploratory probes only; do not assume they expose meaningful content unless they resolve during the run.
Because the fixture shows no console or network errors, focus critique on usability, accessibility, and state clarity rather than error recovery from failed loads.

ux_notes: Scroll successfully exposed the mid-list alarm rows on mobile, confirming the table remains readable after the filter strip and that row selection is available via checkboxes.
Acknowledge-selected action stays pinned at the top while the list scrolls, which supports bulk triage even in the dense mobile layout.
The visible rows show truncated right-side rule text and narrow columns, so scanability may degrade as more of each alarm’s details move off-screen.
Mobile touch ergonomics still look uneven: the top-bar icon and several nav targets are below the 44px guidance, and the severity/status selects remain unlabeled in the accessibility summary.

step.objective: Learn whether the Alarms badge/navigation control opens a meaningful destination or communicates state clearly on mobile, adding one more mobile interaction and coverage signal.
step.success_criteria: The app should either navigate to a distinct page/state or visibly confirm that the alarms control is merely a navigation anchor; either outcome adds UX evidence about orientation and affordance.

ux_notes: Clicking the Alarms badge did navigate to a distinct Alarms page (`alarms.html`) rather than staying on a placeholder state, so the control has clear destination affordance.
The page communicates live state well on mobile: headline counts show ACTIVE 8, CRITICAL 2, and a last refresh timestamp, which helps orientation.
Mobile ergonomics show some friction in the top navigation: several tap targets are under the 44px guidance, including the active Alarms tab and theme toggle.
There are unlabeled filter controls on the Alarms page; the Severity and Status selects triggered missing-label warnings, which weakens accessibility and control clarity.
